data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms as a non-inductive 'critical preference' grounded in the logic of situational analysis, not probability; however, accepting this defense costs the agent any rational assurance that the preferred theory will succeed in the future, reducing scientific action to a bold gamble without epistemic safety nets.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the agent requires a probabilistic guarantee of success before acting, Popper's framework cannot provide it, rendering the preference useless for risk-averse decision making.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) is proven unmeasurable or logically incoherent within Popper's own system, the rationale for preferring one unfalsified theory over another collapses into arbitrary convention.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distinction between 'psychological expectation' and 'rational choice' cannot be maintained in practice, the preference secretly relies on the very inductive habit Popper sought to eliminate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'inductive inference' (claiming future success based on past frequency) and 'critical preference' (choosing the theory that has withstood the most severe tests because it is currently the best candidate for truth, despite no guarantee). The preference is rational because it maximizes informational content and error-elimination potential, not because it predicts success. The cost is the admission that acting on the best-corroborated theory is logically indistinguishable from acting on a known falsehood if both have survived tests so far; the only difference is the depth of the attempt to falsify them.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
